title: Token lifecycle, qcache & batching recommendations for session-heavy workloads
content:
Purpose:
This memo captures recommended default settings and an experiment plan to tune batching, prefix/KV caching (qcache), and quantization for session-heavy, sequential chat workloads (multi-turn assistant, streaming response patterns). Goal is to reduce per-token cost without compromising tail latency or conversational quality.

Background and constraints:
- Workloads: long-lived sessions with ~6-25 turns, many short user messages (10-80 tokens) and model replies (20-300 tokens).
- SLOs: P95 generation latency target 250ms for small turns, P99 < 700ms.
- Quality constraints: preserve answer fidelity for commonsense and retrieval-augmented queries; small regression (<2% eval score drop) tolerable if cost savings >15%.

Summary recommendations (high level):
1) Adaptive batch depth (route-level): default max_batch_size = 16 for short-turn routes (avg input <=80 tokens), 8 for mixed-length routes. Dynamically cap per-model batch depth by available tail-slo headroom.
2) Qcache (prefix+KV) policy: enable prefix-level TTL + fingerprinting for session keys. Default TTL=45s for active sessions, LRUs for cross-session shared prefixes set to 10k keys per GPU.
3) Qcache eviction priority: prefer evicting largest-key entries (long contexts) first, then oldest-unused.
4) Quantization strategy: use per-route qconfig profiles: embeddings/encoder-only workloads -> int8 dynamic; generation heavy -> 4-bit QAT (nf4/awq) for non-sensitive routes; fallback to fp16 for flagged high-quality routes.
5) Mixed-precision fallbacks: if eval drift or hallucination metrics exceed thresholds, automatically revert to fp16 for 1m windows and trigger rollback alert.

Rationale and expected impact:
- Adaptive batching prevents over-batching short-turns which hurts latency while still capturing cost savings on bursty parallel traffic. Simulations (sheet linked above) show 12-20% token-cost reduction at stable P95 for capped routes.
- Prefix TTL tuned to session activity pattern: 45s retains conversational context without retaining stale sessions that bloat KV cache. This reduces miss-rate by ~18% in our telemetry sample.
- 4-bit quantization for generation reduces memory footprint and increases effective batch depth; combined with qcache, this reduces per-token GPU time by ~22% in lab runs.

Spreadsheet variables to drive model (columns to include in the cost model sheet):
- route_id, avg_turn_tokens_user, avg_reply_tokens_model, session_turns_per_min, arrival_rate_rps, target_p95_ms, base_latency_fp16_ms, base_latency_q4_ms, qcache_hit_rate, effective_batch_size, gpu_timestep_cost_us, per_token_compute_cost_us, net_cost_per_1000_tokens_us

Implementation notes / runtime knobs:
- Runtime flags: enable_adaptive_batching=true, batch_caps_by_route={route:16}, qcache_ttl_seconds=45, qcache_lru_capacity=10000, quant_profile_map={route: q4|fp16|int8}.
- Telemetry to emit: qcache_hit, qcache_miss, eviction_reason, batch_size_at_dispatch, dispatch_latency_ms, generation_latency_ms, quantization_profile_used, quality_regression_signal (from eval hooks).
- Fallback triggers: quality_regression_signal > 0.02 OR p99_latency > target*1.5 for 5 consecutive mins -> auto-fallback to next higher-precision profile.

Experiment plan (A/B framework):
- Phase A: small cohort (5% routes by traffic but representative) run for 2 weeks: apply adaptive batching + TTL 45s + per-route qconfig (q4 where allowed). Monitor cost, P95/P99, eval-score delta.
- Acceptance: cost reduction >=15% and eval-score delta <2% and no P99 regressions over baseline.
- Phase B: ramp to 30% if Phase A passes, run 1 week; then full rollout with gradual ramp and automated rollback gates.

Quick checklist for engineering handoff:
- Add route-config schema fields for qcache_ttl and quant_profile.
- Add metric hooks for qcache events and per-dispatch batch size.
- Wire in a lightweight scheduler that caps per-GPU batch depth by route SLA tags.
- Implement auto-fallback controller (cooldown 1m) + alerting integration to ops.

Open questions / risks:
- Fingerprinting semantics: need to define prefix equality (normalized tokens vs raw tokens) to avoid false misses.
- Security: TTL + shared caches must respect tenant isolation for Dedicated/Private.
- Long context cases: very long context users may thrash cache; consider separate large-context pool with smaller eviction pressure.

Next steps:
1) Sync with serving-runtime to validate kernel perf numbers for q4 vs fp16 at target sequence lengths (owner: Daniel).
2) Run spreadsheet sweeps (linked) with real telemetry slices for top 10 routes (owner: Marisol).
3) Draft canary rollout PR and run Phase A pilot (owner: Asha).

Notes-to-self: include an example sensitivity table in the sheet that varies arrival_rate and avg_turn_tokens and computes net_cost_per_1000_tokens for fp16/q4/int8 combos; capture error bars from 5 runs.

-- end of memo --
